title: PM's 8AM Class
text: It's 8AM. Outside, the Saclay wind is trying to remove your eyebrows. Inside, PM is already writing on the board, cheerful, as if 8AM were a reasonable time for anything. Do you go?
speaker: pm

hints: The professor is only ever called PM. First of three 8AM classes: keep it light.

effects.text: PM nods at you. You take notes. Some of them are even legible.

choices.label: Skip, sleep
choices.hint: Your duvet makes a strong case

effects.text: You sleep until 11. Somewhere, PM writes something important on the board.

title: RER B, Somewhere
text: The RER B stops between two stations. Again. A voice mumbles something about an 'incident' and 'a few minutes', which everyone knows means forty. Your phone is at 60%.

effects.text: By the time the train moves, you understand gradient descent. And despair.
A podcast about octopuses. A grey suburb. Strangely, peace.
You emerge knowing everything about a celebrity divorce and nothing about your exam.

title: Sète Tonight?
text: It's Thursday. The group chat is on fire: 'sète tonight, theme is Y2K, no excuses'. You have a problem set due tomorrow and exactly one clean shirt. Are you going?

choices.label: Go
choices.hint: The night is young, so are you

effects.text: The playlist is 2004, the dance moves are worse, the vibe is perfect.
You finish the problem set at 11PM and see the photos at 11:05PM. Mixed feelings.

title: 3AM
text: It's 3AM. The music is still going but you're outside, deep in a great conversation with someone you just met, about AI, free will and the best kebab in Cergy. Your phone is at 4%. Do you go home?
speaker: stranger_3am

hints: Never gender the stranger (Noa). If the player stays, this person can come back at 30.

effects.text: You say goodbye, swap nothing, and sleep like a stone. Some conversations stay one-offs.
The sun comes up over the car park. You've swapped numbers, playlists and one very strong opinion on pineapple pizza.

title: Rent Is Due
text: Your bank app greets you with a red number. Rent is due, the canteen card is empty and pasta has become a personality. Something has to give.

ai.tone: honest about money stress, never pitying

effects.text: You learn to carry four plates and a smile. Your Sunday problem sets suffer.
A sixteen-year-old finally gets derivatives. You get paid and a warm glow.

success.text: Grades check passed: the grant comes through. You buy vegetables, as a treat.

failure.text: Rejected for a missing form you never received. Classic.

title: What Do You Even Do?
text: Christmas dinner. Between the starter and the bûche, an uncle asks: 'So, AIDAMS, is that the computers or the business thing?' Everyone turns to you, forks in the air.

hints: Use the player's origin for the family setting.

effects.text: By the end, your grandmother understands neural networks better than your uncle. Victory.
Your uncle nods with respect. Your cousin rolls their eyes so hard it makes a sound.
Nobody can argue with a good Comté. The subject changes to the weather.

title: PM's 8AM, Again
text: 8AM again. Year 2, same room, same squeaky marker. PM greets a half-empty amphitheatre with suspicious enthusiasm and a slide titled 'This will be on the exam'. Do you go?
speaker: pm

variants.text: 8AM again. Last time you skipped, PM said 'we missed you' to the whole room while looking straight at your empty seat. Today's slide is titled 'This will be on the exam'. Do you go?

hints: If flag pm_skipped_1, PM noticed. Escalate gently: this is the second of three.

choices.label: Go
choices.hint: Coffee in one hand, dignity in the other

effects.text: The slide really was on the exam. PM winks at the front row.

choices.label: Skip, again
choices.hint: What's the worst that can happen?

effects.text: You find out later that it was on the exam. All of it.

title: Sète Tonight?
text: Year 2, another Thursday, another theme: 'business casual but make it chaos'. Someone has rented a péniche on the Seine. Your energy bar is blinking orange. Are you in?

variants.text: Of course there's a sète tonight. There's always a sète tonight. People now ask you where it is. Someone has rented a péniche on the Seine and your name is on the guest list twice. Are you in?

effects.text: The péniche sways. So do you.
You're asleep by eleven. Your future self sends a silent thank-you.

title: 3AM, Again
text: 3AM on the edge of the péniche's deck. You're talking with someone about everything and nothing while the Seine pretends to be romantic. Home, or one more hour?
speaker: stranger_3am

variants.text: 3AM again, and guess who's here: the person from that first 3AM conversation. You pick up exactly where you left off, as if no time had passed. Home, or one more hour?

hints: If flag met_3am, this is Noa again: the bond deepens.

effects.text: You catch the first train home and watch the sunrise from a nearly empty carriage.
One more hour turns into breakfast. Some people just make time disappear.

title: PM Looks Straight at You
text: 8AM, last class before the exams. You reach the door at 8:04. PM stops mid-sentence and looks straight at you. The whole amphitheatre turns around. Do you walk in, or quietly disappear?
speaker: pm

variants.text: 8AM, last class before the exams. You're in your usual seat, of course. PM pauses, looks straight at you and says: 'At least someone has been here every single time.' Do you stay for the whole thing?

hints: Third and last 8AM: PM looks straight at the player. PM will remember this for decades.

effects.text: PM gives you a tiny nod. It will matter, years later.
You walk to the front under thirty stares. PM smiles: 'Better late than absent.'
You close the door very softly. PM's eyebrows will remember this.

title: The Anti-Stress Sète
text: Mid-week, exam season, and someone has organised an 'anti-stress sète'. Your liver files a formal objection. Your FOMO overrules it. Do you go?

ai.tone: chaotic, a little worried for the player

effects.text: You relieve so much stress that you can't remember any of it.
Your friends send a video. You watch it from the library, smug and slightly sad.

title: The Rankings Are Out
text: The exchange office publishes the Year 2 rankings. Your average decides which universities you can pick next year. You refresh the page three times before reading it.

variants.text: The rankings are out: top tier. Singapore, Hong Kong, London, Milan and New York are on your list. Your family has already told the neighbours.
The rankings are out: middle tier. Atlanta, Austin, Washington, Rotterdam, Perth or Montréal. The top tier is close enough to see, far enough to sting. There's still the spring.
The rankings are out: the short list. Daejeon or Santiago, unless something changes this spring. Your past sètes look at you from the photo albums.

hints: Grades shaped by PM's 8AM class, sètes and the Year 2 student style.

effects.text: Butter, sugar, acceptance.
You live in the library until June. Your average climbs. Your tan does not.

title: The New Phone Just Dropped
text: The new phone just dropped. It has a fourth camera, a 'pro' button and a colour called Midnight Sage. Yours works perfectly, apart from a crack you stopped noticing months ago. Upgrade?

effects.text: It's beautiful. It is exactly like the old one. You love it.
Last year's model, half the price. Nobody can tell, least of all you.
You buy a cheap case and feel like a financial genius.

title: Exchange Stories
text: Your stories from {city} get more views than anything you've ever posted: night markets, neon, a bowl of noodles at 2AM. Back home your friends are stuck in the library, and someone comments 'are you even studying?'

effects.text: Two hundred likes. Your mum comments a heart and a question about vegetables.
It's 7AM for them and 2PM for you. Everyone is happy and confused.
You order dinner without pointing. The cook applauds. You may cry.

title: Exchange Stories
text: Your stories from {city} get more views than anything you've ever posted: a campus lawn, a skyline, a suspiciously large coffee. Back home your friends are stuck in the library, and someone comments 'are you even studying?'

effects.text: Two hundred likes. Your mum comments a heart and a question about vegetables.
Everyone talks at once. Your dog barks at the screen. Perfect call.
You top the class project. You post nothing about it, which is the real flex.

title: Forum Entreprises
text: The forum entreprises: two hundred stands, free tote bags and recruiters who say 'we're like a family' with a straight face. You have three hours and one good shirt.

footprint.label: Forum goodies (tote bags, bottles, stress balls)

effects.text: You leave with nine tote bags, four bottles and a stress ball shaped like a cloud server.
A recruiter writes 'promising' on your CV. You can see it upside down. You'll take it.

choices.label: Skip it, go for a run

effects.text: The plateau is all yours. The wind applauds.

title: The Group Chat Drama
text: The AIDAMS group chat explodes at 11PM: someone forgot someone's birthday, someone else posted a political take, and now there are two rival chats and a poll. Your phone buzzes like an angry bee.

hints: Name old friends from the asso or the roommate Lou if known.

effects.text: Your eleven-minute voice note reunites the chats. Someone calls you 'the UN'.
You come back to 1,400 messages and a new group name you don't understand.

choices.label: Screenshot it to the other chat

effects.text: The screenshot travels. You are now the main character, and not in a good way.

title: Ski Trips Every Winter?
text: Your colleagues have a chalet plan: every February, same resort, same fondue, same knee injury from 2019. They want you in, for good. The group chat already has a name.

footprint.label: Yearly ski trips by car (lifts, chalet, design estimate)

effects.text: You become an expert in fondue and a solid intermediate on red slopes.

footprint.label: Occasional ski trips by train (design estimate)

effects.text: You fall asleep in Paris and wake up with snow at the window. Best alarm clock ever.
Every February you get forty photos of fondue. You've made peace with it.

title: The New Phone Just Dropped
text: Another keynote, another phone. This one folds in half, like your resolve. A colleague has already ordered two. Your phone is four years old and only slightly haunted. Upgrade?

effects.text: It folds. You unfold it. You fold it again. This is your life now.

choices.label: Buy a refurbished one
choices.hint: Last year's flagship, half the price

effects.text: Nobody notices. The battery is brand new. You feel smug for a full week.
A new battery for the price of a lunch. Your phone purrs like new.

title: Adopt a Pet?
text: The shelter's page is a wall of hopeful eyes. One of them has a crooked ear and your name written all over it. Your flat is small, your heart is not.

effects.text: Your dog eats a shoe on day one and your heart by day two.

footprint.label: Your cat's food and care (design estimate)

effects.text: Your cat ignores you for a week, then sleeps on your keyboard during an important call.
You water your plants and tell them about your day. They don't wag.

title: The New Phone Just Dropped
text: The new phone just dropped, with an AI that 'understands your mood'. Your current one is so old that teenagers ask if it's 'vintage'. Upgrade?

effects.text: Your new phone says you seem tired. It's right, which is the worst part.
Your phone is older than some of your colleagues' careers. You've never bought a new one on a whim, and you never will.
You keep it. A teenager calls it 'retro'. You decide that's a compliment.

title: Clean Up the Cloud?
text: Your grandchild says deleting your 40,000 cloud photos and 90,000 old emails would 'save the planet'. You have a free afternoon and a slightly guilty conscience. Do you hit delete?

variants.text: Your neighbour's teenager says deleting your 40,000 cloud photos and 90,000 old emails would 'save the planet'. You have a free afternoon and a slightly guilty conscience. Do you hit delete?

hints: The point: it's negligible compared with flights or devices.

effects.text: Gone: the exchange, the weddings, the cat. Saved: about the emissions of a short car trip.
You spend the afternoon scrolling through your life instead. It was a good one, mostly.

title: Grounded
text: Clearing out a drawer, you find your old passport, barely stamped. You've seen the world by train, bus, bike and night ferry. You never once needed a boarding pass.

effects.text: A whole life without flying. Not a sacrifice, it turns out: a style.

title: The Brutal Maths Exam
text: Linear algebra midterm, tomorrow, 8AM. Rumour says last year's average was 6/20 and someone cried in the second row. Your notes are a crime scene. How do you prepare?

hints: Skill check: name it in the narration (Intelligence or Charisma).

success.text: Maths exam: your Intelligence carried you. 15/20, and you understood the last question.

failure.text: Maths exam: your Intelligence ran out at 4AM. 7/20, and the second-row tradition continues.

success.text: Study group: your Charisma kept six people focused for five hours. Everyone passes. You're a legend.

failure.text: Study group: it became a gossip session by 9PM. Great evening, terrible exam.

choices.label: Sleep and accept your fate
choices.hint: A rested brain is a brain

effects.text: You sleep nine hours and guess with confidence. 10/20. Honestly? A win.

title: The Group Project
text: Group project, four people, three working. Your teammate Hugo has contributed one slide titled 'Conclusion (to do)' and a thumbs-up emoji. The deadline is Friday. What do you do?

hints: The free-rider's name can change; keep it light and never cruel.

effects.text: You write the whole thing at 2AM. Hugo presents the conclusion. Confidently.

success.text: Charisma check passed: Hugo apologises, writes a brilliant section and buys everyone crêpes.

failure.text: Charisma check failed: Hugo calls you 'intense' in the group chat. The project is fine. The chat is not.

effects.text: The professor adjusts the grades. Hugo gets the message. So does the rest of the year group.

title: Hackathon Weekend
text: Forty-eight hours, one theme ('AI for good, but make it profitable'), free pizza and a sleeping bag under the desk. Your team has an idea, a name and absolutely no code. Go?

hints: Math & AI skill check. Callback to the AI club if flag TECH.

success.text: Math & AI check passed: your demo works exactly once, live, in front of the jury. First prize and a job card in your pocket.

failure.text: Math & AI check failed: the demo crashes on stage. The jury applauds your 'resilience'. You learned more than the winners.

effects.text: You write two lines of code and eat eleven slices. Networking, technically.
You sleep, run and call your family. The winners' photo is everywhere on Monday.

title: Model UN Night
text: The debate club needs a last-minute delegate for a Model UN on AI regulation. You represent a small island nation with no data centres and very strong opinions. The room is full.

success.text: Debate check passed: Intelligence and Charisma win the room. Your amendment passes, 34 to 2.

failure.text: Debate check failed: you confuse two treaties on the mic. The room laughs. You'll laugh too, in about a year.

effects.text: You broker a deal between three superpowers during the coffee break. Nobody saw it. Everyone felt it.
You watch from the back. Someone else becomes the island nation, very loudly.

title: Interview Week
text: Before the offers, the tests. Recruiters want a case, a coding exercise, a quant puzzle or a panel interview. You have one week and enough energy to prepare one properly. Which one do you go all in on?

ai.tone: nervous, competitive, satirical about recruitment rituals
hints: Each option is a skill check; passing unlocks prestigious employers at the next step.

choices.label: Consulting case interview
choices.hint: Market sizing and a firm handshake

success.text: Case interview: your Economics and Charisma carried you. 'How many croissants are sold in Paris a day?' You nailed it, and the partner smiled.

failure.text: Case interview: your Economics wobbled on the market sizing. You estimated more croissants than people on Earth.

choices.label: Big Tech coding interview
choices.hint: A whiteboard and a ticking clock

success.text: Coding interview: your Math & AI carried you. You reverse the binary tree, then explain why nobody should ever have to.

failure.text: Coding interview: Math & AI check failed. An off-by-one error, live, with the interviewer gently nodding. You'll dream of it.

success.text: Quant test: Intelligence and Math & AI carried you. You price the dice game in your head and they stop the clock early.

failure.text: Quant test failed: the dice game had three dice, not two. You notice on the train home.

success.text: Policy panel: your Intelligence and Charisma carried you. A grey-haired diplomat writes 'sharp' on a napkin.

failure.text: Policy panel: you blank on the question about the precautionary principle. The panel is very polite about it, which is worse.

title: Flat Hunting in Paris
text: Your new salary meets the Paris rental market. Twenty-two square metres, 'charming' (no lift, sixth floor), €1,350 a month, forty people at the viewing. Then a listing appears that's half the price, and the landlord is 'abroad'.

hints: Intelligence check on the too-good listing (deposit scam).

choices.label: Wire the deposit for the deal

success.text: Intelligence check passed: you ask for a video call, check the land registry, and it's real. A rare unicorn: a fair landlord.

failure.text: Intelligence check failed: the landlord was 'abroad' indeed, with your €2,700. The flat never existed.

effects.text: Three flatmates, one bathroom, a passive-aggressive whiteboard. One of them becomes a lifelong friend.
A balcony, a second room and seventy minutes each way. You finish a lot of audiobooks.

choices.label: Back to your parents' for a year

effects.text: Your childhood bedroom, a salary, and a parent who asks 'so, when are you moving out?' every Sunday.

title: Your First Payslip
text: Your first real payslip: forty lines of acronyms, a gross salary that made you proud and a net salary that makes you sit down. Then the tax office sends a friendly email. What now?

hints: Gross vs net shock, French payroll humour.

effects.text: An automatic transfer on the 1st. You forget it exists. In ten years, you'll remember with joy.
A very good dinner and a very nice jacket. Rent day arrives with a raised eyebrow.

choices.label: Learn how taxes and investing work

effects.text: You finally understand your payslip, your pension and why your uncle talks about index funds at every dinner.

title: The Annual Review
text: Annual review. Your manager opens with 'great year!' and a 1.5% raise, 'because of the context'. You know what your colleague earns. You have prepared. Sort of.
speaker: first_manager

hints: Charisma check: name it. Bertrand the first manager may be the one across the table.

success.text: Salary negotiation: your Charisma closed it. Twelve percent and a title with 'Senior' in it.

failure.text: Salary negotiation: Charisma check failed. You get 'we'll revisit in six months', the corporate cousin of 'no'.

success.text: Network check passed: a rival offer appears, your manager panics, your salary jumps.

failure.text: Network check failed: three interviews, zero offers, and you have to pretend you were at the dentist.

effects.text: You thank them for the 1.5%. Inflation thanks you too.

title: Buy or Rent?
text: Your banker, your parents and three podcasts agree: 'renting is throwing money away'. Your spreadsheet disagrees. The flat you love has a 25-year mortgage attached. The suburbs have a garden.

hints: Economics check on the renting-and-investing option.

choices.label: Buy the flat in the city

effects.text: You get the keys and a mortgage the length of your career. You paint the walls a colour called 'Ambition'.

footprint.label: Suburban house and two cars (heating, driving, design estimate)

effects.text: A lawn, a barbecue, a garage for two cars and forty minutes of traffic each way. Weekends are glorious.

success.text: Economics check passed: your index funds quietly outrun the property market. Your banker stops calling.

failure.text: Economics check failed: you 'invest the difference' in takeaway food and a new sofa.
